clue.text: Bishop goes on march to disband the army

indicators.note: goes on means the bishop's letter is placed after the march

parts.note: a protest march is a demo
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop joins a protest march calling for the army to be disbanded.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is to discharge troops from military service, informal short for demobilise.

clue.text: The deep ______ of his taking-off" (Macbeth)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Macbeth's soliloquy about murdering Duncan

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth, Act 1 Scene 7: Duncan's virtues will plead against 'the deep damnation of his taking-off', meaning his murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the eternal punishment Macbeth fears for killing the king.

clue.text: Castle, perhaps, or imposing sort of house

parts.note: a castle or rook is an example of a chess man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A castle, or else some kind of grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castle' looks like the definition but is a chess piece, a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor house is the large country residence of an estate's lord.

clue.text: Objection over masses of badges

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the objection above the masses

parts.note: but is a word raising an objection, as in 'no buts'
tons means masses, lots

explanation.surface: Someone protests at piles of badges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapel buttons are small pin-on badges, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Capital sum for headmaster

explanation.surface: The capital sum paid to a head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal is the original sum of a loan before interest, and also the head of a school or college.

clue.text: A godfather going round the sacred building

indicators.note: going round means the father's letters enclose the others

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A godparent walks around a holy building.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'godfather' looks like one unit, a sponsor at a christening, but it splits into god and father; 'going round' has the parent wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered temple tower in Buddhist and Hindu traditions.

clue.text: Key to fire engine?

parts.note: suggests a key for a fire brigade's vehicle, but means the key that sets a motor firing

explanation.walkthrough: Fire here is a verb: the key that makes an engine fire, start up.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting system of a car sparks the fuel and is switched on with a key.

clue.text: About the right amount to fill a bus

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: the quantity that fills one

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
a load is an amount carried

explanation.surface: Roughly how many people a bus will hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Bus is old slang for a car, so its full load fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The quantity a motor vehicle can carry, bus being slang for a car.

clue.text: He was told not to work in Askelon

definitions.text: He was told not to work in Askelon

parts.words: He was told not to work in Askelon
parts.note: alludes to David's lament in 2 Samuel: 'Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon'

explanation.walkthrough: The Bible line 'publish it not in the streets of Askelon' is read as an order to someone whose job is publishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose trade is to publish was the one forbidden to do so in that city.

clue.text: Being found untruthful

explanation.surface: Discovered to be telling lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means situated (as a town lying by a river) and also telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Timely weapon for colonial militiamen?

parts.note: a timely weapon suggests one tied to the clock, and colonial militiamen evokes the American Minutemen, ready at a minute's notice

explanation.walkthrough: A signal gun fired once every minute, for mourning or distress; the Minutemen were the American revolutionary militia, ready to turn out at a minute's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon discharged at sixty-second intervals as a signal is named after that interval of time.

clue.text: Divinity teacher, almost useless at games

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rabbit is British slang for a hopeless player, especially at cricket or tennis

explanation.surface: A theology teacher who is hopeless at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher of religious law.

clue.text: Publication's admission of complaint improves the atmosphere

indicators.note: admission means letting something in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: airing a view is making it public, so publication is an airing
a complaint in the medical sense is a condition or ailment

explanation.surface: A magazine's admission that it was wrong clears the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the answer does: a system that improves the air indoors. 'Complaint' is an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling and ventilating equipment makes a room's air fresher and more comfortable.

clue.text: Devilish One's in slow motion

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in means the short verb sits inside the speed unit

parts.note: motion measured in miles per hour, abbreviated mph
the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A mischievous person moves in slow motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' does double duty in letters: One gives I, and its 's stands for IS, which goes inside MPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means mischievous like a small demon or sprite.

clue.text: Possibility of excellent rise in strong pound

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: potent means strong
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: The chance of a fine rise in a strong pound sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is spelt with the letter I for the figure; 'rise' turns it upwards in this down clue, giving IA, and 'in' sets that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Potential is latent capacity, something that may come to be.

clue.text: It contained something nasty in Cold Comfort Farm

definitions.text: It contained something nasty in Cold Comfort Farm

parts.words: It contained something nasty in Cold Comfort Farm
parts.note: recalls the famous line in Stella Gibbons's comic novel where Aunt Ada Doom saw something nasty in a garden outbuilding

explanation.walkthrough: In Stella Gibbons's novel Cold Comfort Farm, Aunt Ada Doom never recovered from seeing 'something nasty' in a rustic outbuilding as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut for storing firewood is the setting of the novel's running joke.

clue.text: Land on the Continent in depression is discouraging

indicators.note: in means the French word goes inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
terre is French for land

explanation.surface: Arriving in a gloomy Europe is disheartening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood; it is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent measure is one that puts people off acting.

clue.text: Used to speak highly of latest fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Once given to praising the newest trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to speak highly' looks like 'once praised'; it means a voice pitched high.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is the high voice a male singer or speaker uses above his natural range.

clue.text: No army, head is penniless

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: With no army, the leader is broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Having not a bean is the idiom for owning no money at all.

clue.text: They are born, it's ordered, to be free forever

definitions.text: They are born, it's ordered, to be free forever

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: People born under a decree that they stay free.
explanation.walkthrough: Rule, Britannia! declares 'Britons never, never, never shall be slaves', so the whole clue describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Britain are, by the patriotic song, decreed never to be enslaved.

clue.text: Private hours of prayer rejected "

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: terce is one of the canonical hours of prayer, so several are terces

explanation.surface: A private person turns down the set times of prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept private is hidden from others, confidential.

clue.text: Old urge to fast

parts.note: ex means former, old
to press is to urge

explanation.surface: An old urge to go without food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like going without food; it means speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train or delivery is a rapid one.

clue.text: Mangle the French under garment

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the French word beneath the clothing

parts.note: garb is clothing
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Wringing out a French undergarment in a mangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mangle' looks like a laundry wringer; it means distort.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble a message is to jumble and distort it.

clue.text: Writer's device for emphasising a point

definitions.text: Writer's device for emphasising a point

parts.words: Writer's device for emphasising a point
parts.note: seems a rhetorical trick for stressing an argument, but the writer is a writing implement whose tip is honed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Emphasising a point' suggests rhetoric; here the point is the tip of a pencil and emphasising means making it sharper.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bladed gadget shaves wood and graphite to give a pencil a fine tip.

clue.text: With prunes, pronounced good for the lips in Little Dorrit

definitions.text: With prunes, pronounced good for the lips in Little Dorrit

parts.words: With prunes, pronounced good for the lips in Little Dorrit
parts.note: in Dickens's novel Mrs General recommends saying 'papa, potatoes, poultry, prunes and' a final word to shape the lips

explanation.walkthrough: Mrs General in Little Dorrit advises 'Papa, potatoes, poultry, prunes, and prism are all very good words for the lips'.
explanation.definitionFit: The last word of Mrs General's lip-forming list is the glass optical solid.

clue.text: Tinny alarm reveals presence of wild animal

indicators.note: reveals means the animal shows itself within the run of words

explanation.surface: A tinny alarm warns that a wild beast is near.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Time to face the bowling, as Jones might say

definitions.text: Time to face the bowling, as Jones might say

parts.words: Time to face the bowling, as Jones might say
parts.note: a batsman going out to bat would say '...', and run together that is the first name of the architect Jones

explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect; in cricket, a batsman goes 'in' to face the bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo is the forename of the architect Jones, and also reads as a batsman's 'in I go'.

clue.text: China let a war be concealed

indicators.note: concealed suggests the letters are disguised, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: China allowed a war to be kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but means crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain crockery, and tableware covers dishes and plates used for meals.

clue.text: It shows how far it is for the old soldier to Durham, perhaps

definitions.text: It shows how far it is for the old soldier to Durham, perhaps

parts.words: It shows how far it is for the old soldier to Durham, perhaps
parts.note: reads as a roadside marker telling a weary veteran the distance to a town; miles is also Latin for soldier

explanation.walkthrough: A roadside stone marks the distance to a town such as Durham; the 'old soldier' hints at Latin miles, the Roman soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside marker post records the distance to a named town.

clue.text: Old black king in place of Lear's Akond?.

indicators.note: in means the king's letter goes inside the place name

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote the nonsense poem The Akond of Swat
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An old dark-skinned king occupies the realm of Lear's Akond.
explanation.definitionFit: Swart is an archaic word for dark or dusky.
